_comment: Pass lines are per index. A pass line measured on one index says nothing about another: the corpora differ in what they contain, so the population differs. v8b -- the corpus behind this index had no item-level (号) or sub-item text, and branch-numbered articles (e.g. 132-2) were absent from the index entirely; kept so that selecting the v8b index still reproduces the historical numbers. v9 -- item and sub-item text is first-class; branch-numbered articles are present; the fidelity gates pass with zero violations. The v9 numbers are lower than v8b's. They are the pass line anyway: the index is more correct, and a pass line exists to detect drift, not to flatter the build. This file is anchored by an out-of-repo digest (see tools/scripts/verify-gates-lock.py); values here are owner-locked baselines and must not be edited to make a run pass. The honbun N is not the full question set: a question is scored only when its gold articles exist in both this corpus and an older corpus used as a cross-filter, and the older corpus lacks branch-numbered articles, so those questions are dropped before scoring. This pass line is therefore provisional -- once that cross-filter is removed it will be re-measured against the full set and the numbers will move. It still does its job here (a fixed denominator detects drift), but it is not a statement about overall accuracy.

v0.2-aug-v8b-gemini.note: measured on the index built before item-level chunks existed
